newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money unchanged in 4th session.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money unchanged in 4th session.

text.p: ---------------------- Feb 20 -------------------------- *Central Bank keeps overnight borrowing at 10.5 pct
Manila overnight money continued to be anchored at an average of 10.5625 percent for the fourth straight session on Thursday due to a dearth of borrowers in the market, traders said.
Rates were contained in a narrow band from 10.625 to 10.53125 percent, with 24 lenders and 15 borrowers.
Volume narrowed to 7.611 billion from 18.424 billion pesos.
"It's the middle of the week. Banks are just staying square," a foreign bank dealer said, referring to the smaller market volume.
Banks continued to have a high level of liquidity since they have stayed away from term reverse repos which carry a 20 percent tax.
Meanwhile, banks were investing their money in short-term bills to park their excess liquidity. They have also been buying these bills to service their clients' requirements, traders said.
According to a Reuter poll of seven financial insitutions, they gave bid rates of 10.665 to 10.70 percent on the 91-day bills.
